observations: Single photo shows a used automatic transmission/gearbox assembly sitting on a dirty workshop floor.
Background shows other disassembled engine parts and water bottles, consistent with a used-parts yard.
A watermark reads 'MR QUALITY PARTS' - this is the seller's shop branding, not a part or vehicle brand.
No vehicle make, model, or part number plate is legible anywhere in the image.
Surface shows grease, grime, and some corrosion/staining; one bolt area shows wear.
Torque converter face is visible but its condition (seals, splines) cannot be judged from a static photo.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows only an exterior, grimy static shot; no way to confirm internal or functional condition.
No documentation, receipt, or shop signage shown in photo 0 to confirm a warranty policy exists.

risks.risk: Vehicle fitment (make/model/engine code) is unknown, which drives price heavily for a transmission.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the part/tag number stamped or labeled on the transmission casing, or a photo of the donor vehicle.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all without this - fitment-specific pricing is impossible

risks.risk: Internal gear/clutch pack or torque converter condition unknown; could be worn, damaged, or seized.
risks.proof: Video of the transmission being tested/turned on a bench or in a running vehicle, or a borescope/teardown photo.

risks.risk: Fluid leaks from seals or gaskets not assessable from a single static photo.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all seal and gasket areas, ideally after wiping clean.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming leaks present, needing reseal

risks.risk: Mileage or accident history of the donor vehicle is unknown.
risks.proof: Photo of VIN tag or donor vehicle registration paperwork.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unknown history, high-mileage assumption

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the part number/tag on the transmission case to confirm vehicle fitment.
Video of the unit being tested (e.g., spun by hand, or bench-tested with power) showing it engages without noise.
Close-up photos of all seals and the torque converter area for leak/wear signs.
Any paperwork or photo evidence supporting the 6-month warranty claim.
response.reason: A transmission's price depends entirely on which vehicle/engine it fits, and no part number or model is readable in the single photo provided, so even a worst-case price cannot be set.
